text:
Jason Robertson scored three goals in 5:20 of the second period, and Dallas needed every one of them. The Stars led 4-0 by the 6-minute mark, then watched Washington score five times before the horn and fall a goal short, 6-5. Robertson's second and third came on 3% looks from our chance model, the kind of shots that rarely go in, and Dallas had little trouble turning them into a cushion. Drafted 39th overall in 2017 out of Kingston, he finished with three goals and an assist, and Roope Hintz added a goal and two assists. Mikko Rantanen also reached 800 career points with his assist-free goal in the second.

The game was closer than the early score suggested. Washington took 58 shot attempts to Dallas's 47 and had a slight edge in expected goals (the quality of chances) in the second period, 1.23 to 1.12. Overall, Dallas led it 3.15 to 2.91. Our simulation of every shot, the share of replays each team wins, gave Dallas 54% and Washington 46%, so the Stars were not far from deserving it. Logan Thompson allowed four goals on 11 shots, about 2.7 more than his chances called for, and Charlie Lindgren stopped nine of 11 in relief. Jordan Kyrou had a goal and two assists, and Ryan Leonard, the No. 8 pick in 2023, scored a goal with 1:02 left to make it 6-5. Jake Oettinger faced 25 shots and allowed five.

Our facts don't include streaks or standings, so we can only say this: Dallas escaped a rally that nearly erased a four-goal lead, and Washington lost despite out-attempting the Stars and scoring five goals.
